newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Israeli mutual funds post inflow in February.
newsitem.headline: Israeli mutual funds post inflow in February.

text.p: Israeli mutual funds posted a net inflow of money in February for the second month in a row after three years of steady net redemptions, Meitav Investments and Securities said in a report released on Thursday.

Israel's 310 mutual funds took in a net 373 million shekels in February, compared with 141 million in January. Combined with the funds' 2.1 percent return, total assets rose 4.6 percent to 15.33 billion shekels at the end of February, Meitav said.
Shekel funds led the inflow, registering a net intake of 277 million shekels. Share funds took in 55 million shekels and bond funds 42 million.
Meitav, a brokerage house and fund manager that tracks the mutual fund industry, said the influx reflected continued good performance of the stock and bond markets.
"During February share prices reached an all-time record high - 277.73 points in the Maof index, amid a big increase in turnover that reached 200 million shekels a day," Meitav said.
"Towards the end of the month, after political developments in the Bar-On affair and declines on Wall Street, big declines were registered," Meitav said.
